prompt.context_jp: 建築家として長年精進を重ねてきた桑野信介にとって、自宅の玄関に締め出されるという事態___、この上なく屈辱的なものである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 建築家として長年精進を重ねてきた桑野信介にとって、自宅の玄関に締め出されるという事態___、この上なく屈辱的なものである。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that marks the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: The sentence makes a judgment about 'being locked out' as a topic (it is humiliating). は sets up that topic for commentary.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present it as new information identifying what is humiliating, but the narrator is characterizing an already-established situation. を doesn't fit this predicate structure.

contrast_examples.jp: 屈辱的なのはこの事態だ。
contrast_examples.en: What's humiliating is this situation. (identification with が/のは)

prompt.context_jp: 若い娘の一言で疑い___晴れる有り様は、日頃の彼の誇りからすれば不本意極まりない。
prompt.prompt_jp: 若い娘の一言で疑い___晴れる有り様は、日頃の彼の誇りからすれば不本意極まりない。
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle marking the subject of 晴れる in this relative/nominal clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a noun-modifying clause (有り様 describing the scene), the subject takes が, not は. が describes the event neutrally.
feedback.incorrect_en: は cannot usually appear as the subject marker inside a relative/noun-modifying clause. を would make 晴れる transitive, which it is not here.

contrast_examples.en: He cleared the suspicion. (transitive, uses を)

prompt.context_jp: 「最近 この辺りに 変質者___出没するもんでね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「最近 この辺りに 変質者___出没するもんでね」
prompt.prompt_en: The officer is introducing a new, unidentified entity. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The officer is introducing the existence of a pervert as new information — classic が of neutral description/existence.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would imply the pervert is an already-known topic being commented on, which doesn't match 'there's been a pervert around lately'.

contrast_examples.en: There's a cat over there. (new info)

contrast_examples.jp: あの猫はうちの飼い猫だ。
contrast_examples.en: That cat is our pet. (known topic)

prompt.context_jp: この事務所の仕事___近頃どれも順調で、決して低迷しているわけではない。
prompt.prompt_jp: この事務所の仕事___近頃どれも順調で、決して低迷しているわけではない。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle that sets up 'the work at this office' as the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: The narrator comments on the office's work as a general topic ('as for the work, it's going well'). は is the natural topic marker here.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would narrowly identify which work is going well, suggesting contrast with something else. The sentence is a general assessment, not an identification.

contrast_examples.jp: 仕事が順調なのは、彼のおかげだ。
contrast_examples.en: It's thanks to him that work is going well.

prompt.context_jp: 「お客さまからの要望を 簡単に却下できないでしょう？ お金を出してるの___ お客さまなんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お金を出してるの___ お客さまなんだから」
prompt.prompt_en: Maya is identifying WHO pays. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: The 〜のは〜だ cleft structure uses は on the nominalized clause to identify the client as the one paying. The focus falls on 'お客さま'.
feedback.incorrect_en: が after のを here would be ungrammatical; the cleft requires は. も would mean 'also the client', changing the meaning.

prompt.context_jp: 「花柄___な 俺が この世で 嫌いなトップ5に入るんだよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「花柄___な 俺が この世で 嫌いなトップ5に入るんだよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano singles out floral patterns to contrast with other things. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: は here marks 'floral patterns' as the topic being singled out for emphatic contrast — out of everything, THIS is in his top 5 hates.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce it as new information identifying what is in the top 5, which is less natural for this emphatic, contrastive statement.

contrast_examples.en: Floral is what I hate most. (exhaustive identification)

prompt.context_jp: 「大丈夫よ 狙われるの___ もっと若い子でしょう？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「狙われるの___ もっと若い子でしょう？」
prompt.prompt_en: Natsumi uses a cleft to identify who gets targeted. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: 〜のは〜 cleft: 'the one who gets targeted IS younger girls'. The topic-focus structure requires は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が in this slot breaks the cleft construction. The nominalized clause のは sets up what is being identified.

contrast_examples.jp: 狙われるのは若い子だ。
contrast_examples.en: The ones targeted are young girls.

prompt.context_jp: 仕事___滞るのは、この男にとって最も許しがたいことのはずである。
prompt.prompt_jp: 仕事___滞るのは、この男にとって最も許しがたいことのはずである。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle marking the subject inside this noun-modifying clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside the のは clause, the subject 仕事 takes が — this is the event 'work being delayed' presented neutrally before being made into a topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside a noun-modifying clause is blocked here; the topic marker belongs to のは at the outer level, not to the inner subject.

contrast_examples.en: a day on which it rains

prompt.context_jp: 「自分の意見を通すだけじゃなくて 注文に応じるの___ 建築家の仕事でしょう？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「注文に応じるの___ 建築家の仕事でしょう？」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for this cleft-like structure.

feedback.correct_en: も adds 'responding to requests' to the previous idea ('not only pushing your opinion, BUT ALSO responding'). The 〜だけじゃなくて〜も pattern needs も.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just identify the subject but miss the 'also' sense set up by だけじゃなくて. を doesn't fit this nominalized subject slot.

contrast_examples.jp: 話すだけじゃなく、聞くのも大事だ。
contrast_examples.en: Not only speaking but also listening is important.

prompt.context_jp: 「女性___とって そういうのが どんなに怖いか知らないんですよ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「女性___とって そういうのが どんなに怖いか知らないんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the 〜にとって phrase meaning 'for/to women'.

feedback.correct_en: にとって is a fixed expression meaning 'from the perspective of/for'. The に is required.
feedback.incorrect_en: が or は can't form this fixed phrase; they would break the idiom meaning 'for women'.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供にとって難しい問題

prompt.context_jp: 「桑野さんって ケン___は仲良くなれるのに 人___仲良くなりたいとは 思わないんですか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ケンとは仲良くなれるのに 人___仲良くなりたいとは 思わないんですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Michiru contrasts dogs with people. Pick the particle combo for 'with people'.

feedback.correct_en: 仲良くなる takes と for 'with (someone)'. The は adds contrastive focus: 'but with people, you don't want to...'.
feedback.incorrect_en: がは is ungrammatical. には would suggest direction/location, not the 'with' sense needed for 仲良くなる.

contrast_examples.en: With him, I don't want to talk. (contrastive)

prompt.context_jp: 「あの自転車 昨日の昼間 五反田___ 盗まれたみたいですね」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの自転車 昨日の昼間 五反田___ 盗まれたみたいですね」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the location where the theft happened.

feedback.correct_en: で marks the location where an action takes place. The stealing happened at Gotanda, so で is correct.
feedback.incorrect_en: に would mark a destination or existence location, not the setting of an action. を doesn't fit this passive construction's location.

prompt.context_jp: 理解の及ばぬ相手ほど、人を惹きつけるもの___あるらしい。
prompt.prompt_jp: 理解の及ばぬ相手ほど、人を惹きつけるもの___あるらしい。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle introducing 'something that attracts people' as new information.

feedback.correct_en: 〜がある introduces the existence of something new ('there seems to be something attractive'). This is classic existential が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would presuppose the attractive thing is already known. The narrator is introducing this observation freshly.

contrast_examples.jp: 何か特別なものがある。

prompt.context_jp: 画面に浮かんだ差出人不明のメッセージに、彼女の指先___止まる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 彼女の指先___止まる。
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for the subject in this descriptive, scene-setting sentence.

feedback.correct_en: Narrative description of a sudden event — 'her fingertips stop' — takes が for neutral description of what happens.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make it a topic comment, which clashes with this momentary, observed action in narration.

prompt.context_jp: 「一緒に歩いて何___悪い？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「一緒に歩いて何___悪い？」
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano snaps back. Pick the particle after 何.

feedback.correct_en: 何が悪い is a fixed rhetorical pattern ('what's wrong with it?'). 何 as an unknown subject takes が.
feedback.incorrect_en: Interrogative pronouns like 何 cannot take は as subject — は presupposes known reference, which contradicts a question word.

prompt.context_jp: 「メールの犯人___ 誰なのか そっちのほうが 問題なんじゃないの？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「メールの犯人___ 誰なのか そっちのほうが 問題なんじゃないの？」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the particle for 'who the email culprit is'.

feedback.correct_en: Embedded question: 犯人が誰なのか ('who the culprit is'). The subject inside this embedded question uses が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は inside embedded questions sounds unnatural because the identity hasn't been established — が introduces the unknown subject.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰が犯人なのか分からない。
contrast_examples.en: I don't know who the culprit is.
The culprit is him. (already a topic)

prompt.context_jp: 「彼女の携帯 見たの___ あなたしかいないの」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「彼女の携帯 見たの___ あなたしかいないの」
prompt.prompt_en: Natsumi confronts the mummy. Pick the particle.

feedback.correct_en: Classic 〜のは〜 cleft: 'the one who saw the phone is only you'. は sets up the nominalized topic.
feedback.incorrect_en: が breaks the cleft structure. The sentence identifies the referent of 'the person who saw it'.

contrast_examples.en: The one who did it is him.

prompt.context_jp: 制服の男に自転車泥棒よろしく___られた桑野は、なんとか隣人の口添えで放免となった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 制服の男に自転車泥棒よろしく___られた桑野は、なんとか隣人の口添えで放免となった。
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'suspected/scrutinized'?

feedback.correct_en: 見咎める means to notice someone and challenge/question them with suspicion — exactly what the officer does to Kuwano.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見送る means to see someone off; 見分ける means to distinguish. Neither captures the suspicious challenging.

contrast_examples.en: He was questioned by a policeman.
I saw my friend off at the station.

prompt.context_jp: 「___苦労って やつじゃないのか？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___苦労って やつじゃないのか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase means 'needless worry (about something that may not happen)'?

feedback.correct_en: 取り越し苦労 is the idiom for worrying about things that may never happen. Kuwano is dismissing the stalker fear this way.
feedback.incorrect_en: 持ち越し (carrying over) and 繰り越し (rollover) are unrelated to needless anxiety.

contrast_examples.jp: 問題を来週に持ち越す。
contrast_examples.en: Carry the issue over to next week.

prompt.context_jp: 塵も___ば山となると言うように、この数日の恐怖が彼女の顔を強張らせていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 塵も___ば山となる
prompt.prompt_en: Complete the proverb 'even dust piles up into a mountain'.

feedback.correct_en: The fixed proverb is 塵も積もれば山となる — small things accumulate into something large.
feedback.incorrect_en: 重なる and 集まる can mean similar things in general, but the proverb specifically uses 積もる.

contrast_examples.jp: 塵も積もれば山となる。
contrast_examples.en: Many a little makes a mickle.

prompt.context_jp: 「部下も一緒です これは___なアリバイだ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「これは___なアリバイだ」
prompt.prompt_en: Kuwano boasts about his alibi. Which word fits best?

feedback.correct_en: 完璧なアリバイ ('a perfect alibi') is the standard collocation — 完璧 emphasizes flawlessness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 完全 is grammatical but less idiomatic with アリバイ. 完了 means 'completion' and doesn't fit as a modifier here.

prompt.context_jp: 「いや なんか… 胃が___と痛んで」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「胃が___と痛んで」
prompt.prompt_en: Which mimetic word describes a nagging, twinging stomach pain?

feedback.correct_en: シクシク describes a dull, persistent, nagging pain — typical for stress-related stomach aches, which fits Kuwano here.
feedback.incorrect_en: ズキズキ is a throbbing pain (headaches, wounds). ピリピリ is a sharp tingling/stinging sensation.

contrast_examples.en: My stomach has a dull ache.

prompt.context_jp: 「___だから怒るんでしょう？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___だから怒るんでしょう？」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word means 'hitting the bullseye / exactly right'?

feedback.correct_en: 図星 means 'hitting the nail on the head' — Kuwano is accusing Natsumi of being angry because he's exactly right about her loneliness.
feedback.incorrect_en: 図解 means 'diagram/illustration', 図形 means 'figure/shape'. Neither has the idiomatic 'bullseye' meaning.

contrast_examples.en: He hit the nail on the head.

prompt.context_jp: 「イヤなら___ば よかったじゃないッスか」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「イヤなら___ば よかったじゃないッスか」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb means 'refuse (the work)'?

feedback.correct_en: 断る means 'to refuse/decline (an offer or request)' — the standard verb for turning down work.
feedback.incorrect_en: 切る means to cut; 止める means to stop. Neither captures declining a request.

prompt.context_jp: 「困ってるときは ___」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「困ってるときは ___」
prompt.prompt_en: Which set phrase means 'it's mutual / we help each other'?

feedback.correct_en: お互いさま is the standard response meaning 'we're all in it together / it goes both ways' — used to downplay a favor.
feedback.incorrect_en: お疲れさま acknowledges effort. おかげさま expresses gratitude for someone's support. Neither fits 'when you're in trouble'.

contrast_examples.jp: 困ったときはお互いさまです。
contrast_examples.en: We help each other in hard times.

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano pushes back about walking Michiru home and asks what's in it for him.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for Kuwano's cynical 'what benefit do I get' reply?

choices.text: それをやって 僕に 何かメリットでもあるんですか？
それをやって 僕が 何かメリットでもありますか？
それをやった 僕に 何かメリットがあるんですか？

feedback.correct_en: A is the actual line and uses the natural rhetorical pattern 〜でもあるんですか ('is there even any benefit?'), with に marking the recipient of benefit.
feedback.incorrect_en: B uses が for the beneficiary, which sounds off — benefits accrue 'to' someone (に). C's past tense それをやった changes the meaning to a completed act.

contrast_examples.jp: 私に何かメリットがありますか？
contrast_examples.en: Is there any benefit to me?

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano is shouting at the officer about how women stay vigilant at night.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version is most natural?

choices.text: 夜道 歩くのに 携帯に“110番”って打って いつでも押せるようにして 歩いたりしてるんですよ！
夜道を歩くのに 携帯で“110番”を打って いつでも押すようになって 歩くんですよ！
夜道 歩くのを 携帯に“110番”って打つから いつでも押せて 歩いたりしてるんですよ！

feedback.correct_en: A is the actual line. 携帯に打つ ('type into the phone') uses に for the destination of input, and 押せるようにして naturally expresses 'making it so you can press it anytime'.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 押すようになって means 'becoming able to press', changing the nuance. C's 押せて breaks the purposive construction.

contrast_examples.jp: いつでも使えるようにしておく。
contrast_examples.en: Keep it ready to use anytime.

prompt.context_jp: Michiru confesses her unexpected feelings to Natsumi.
prompt.prompt_en: Which phrasing sounds most natural for 'I might have fallen for Kuwano-san'?

choices.text: 桑野さんのことを 好きになっちゃったかも
桑野さんは 好きになっちゃったかも
桑野さんが 好きになっちゃったかも

feedback.correct_en: A is the actual line. 〜のことを好きになる is the natural collocation for 'come to like/fall for someone', using を with 好きになる.
feedback.incorrect_en: B with は shifts focus awkwardly. C with が would make Kuwano the one doing the liking, flipping the meaning.

contrast_examples.jp: 彼のことを好きになった。
彼が私を好きになった。

prompt.context_jp: Eiji earnestly pleads for Kuwano not to let him go.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds most natural for 'please don't think you can do without me'?

choices.text: 俺のこと いなくていいなんて 思わないでください
俺のこと いなくていいなんて 思ってはいけません
俺のこと いない方がいいって 思えばいいです

feedback.correct_en: A is the actual line. 〜ないでください is the natural, emotional request form from a subordinate to his boss.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 〜てはいけません sounds like a rule/prohibition, too stiff for this plea. C flips the meaning entirely to a suggestion.

prompt.context_jp: Kuwano confronts the stalker and tells him never to approach Michiru again.
prompt.prompt_en: Which version sounds most natural and forceful?

choices.text: 二度と あの子に近づくな！ メールも出すな！
二度と あの子に近づかないな！ メールも出さないな！
二度と あの子に近づくなよ メールも出すなよ

feedback.correct_en: A is the actual line. The bare 〜な prohibition form is the strongest, most direct 'don't' — fitting Kuwano's confrontational moment.
feedback.incorrect_en: B's 近づかないな is ungrammatical as a prohibition. C with よ softens the command, undercutting the urgency.
